parameters.query:
-- STEP 1 — resolve identity on phone (certain match).
-- Creates a customer for any phone we have never seen, then attaches every
-- unlinked interaction carrying that phone.
WITH new_people AS (
  INSERT INTO customers (primary_phone_e164, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
  SELECT DISTINCT i.customer_phone_e164, min(i.started_at), max(i.started_at)
  FROM interactions i
  WHERE i.customer_id IS NULL
    AND i.customer_phone_e164 IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM customers c WHERE c.primary_phone_e164 = i.customer_phone_e164
    )
  GROUP BY i.customer_phone_e164
  ON CONFLICT (primary_phone_e164) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING customer_id, primary_phone_e164
),
ident AS (
  INSERT INTO customer_identities (customer_id, kind, value, method, confidence)
  SELECT customer_id, 'phone'::identity_kind, primary_phone_e164,
         'exact_phone'::match_method, 1.00
  FROM new_people
  ON CONFLICT (kind, value) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING customer_id
)
UPDATE interactions i
SET customer_id = c.customer_id
FROM customers c
WHERE i.customer_id IS NULL
  AND i.customer_phone_e164 = c.primary_phone_e164;

nodes.name: Resolve identity (phone)
nodes.notes: Phone match only — it is the one match that is certain. CRM-id and fuzzy-name matching are deliberately NOT automated: a wrong merge is expensive to undo and every match is written to customer_identities with its method and confidence.

parameters.query:
-- STEP 2 — turn agent promises extracted by pass 1 into follow_up rows,
-- then close any that a later interaction fulfilled.
INSERT INTO follow_ups (customer_id, agent_id, promised_in, promise_text, promised_at, due_at, channel)
SELECT i.customer_id, i.agent_id, i.interaction_id,
       p->>'promise',
       i.started_at,
       CASE WHEN p->>'due_hint' IS NOT NULL THEN i.started_at + interval '24 hours' END,
       i.channel
FROM interaction_analysis ia
JOIN interactions i ON i.interaction_id = ia.interaction_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(
  coalesce(ia.raw_response->'promises_made_by_agent', '[]'::jsonb)) AS p
WHERE i.agent_id IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM follow_ups f
    WHERE f.promised_in = i.interaction_id AND f.promise_text = p->>'promise'
  );

-- STEP 3 — close promises that a later outbound contact fulfilled.
UPDATE follow_ups f
SET fulfilled_in = nxt.interaction_id,
    fulfilled_at = nxt.started_at,
    hours_to_fulfil = round(extract(epoch from (nxt.started_at - f.promised_at))/3600.0, 2),
    status = CASE
      WHEN nxt.started_at <= coalesce(f.due_at, f.promised_at + interval '24 hours')
        THEN 'fulfilled' ELSE 'late' END,
    updated_at = now()
FROM LATERAL (
  SELECT i.interaction_id, i.started_at
  FROM interactions i
  WHERE i.customer_id = f.customer_id
    AND i.started_at > f.promised_at
    AND i.agent_id = f.agent_id
  ORDER BY i.started_at
  LIMIT 1
) nxt
WHERE f.status = 'open';

-- Anything still open past its deadline is a missed promise, not a pending one.
UPDATE follow_ups
SET status = 'missed', updated_at = now()
WHERE status = 'open'
  AND coalesce(due_at, promised_at + interval '48 hours') < now();

nodes.name: Rebuild customer_metrics
nodes.notes: Truncate and rebuild. customer_metrics is fully derived, so it can always be dropped and recomputed — which is what stops a wrong dashboard number from becoming permanent.
